grammar.note: Wie geht es dir? = How are you? Perfekt with sein.
nach Hause = (going) home; zu Hause = at home.
Irregular: du isst, er isst.
Colloquial short form of herein/hinein. As an adjective rein means "pure": reines Wasser.
Mostly in Das stimmt = That’s right. Stimmt so! = Keep the change.
Irregular: du nimmst, er nimmt.
Mixed verb: brachte, gebracht. Someone (dative) something (accusative).

example_target: Kannst du mir ein Glas Wasser [[bringen]]?
example_source: Can you [[bring]] me a glass of water?

grammar.note: Not declined. Comes after adjectives: groß genug = big enough.
nicht brauchen zu = not have to: Du brauchst nicht zu kommen.
With clock times: gegen acht Uhr = around eight o’clock.
im Moment = at the moment.
Weak noun: den/dem/des Jungen. Colloquial plural also die Jungs.

example_source: The [[boy]] is playing in the garden.

grammar.note: Das steht dir gut = That suits you. In southern Germany and Austria: ist gestanden.

example_source: We are [[standing]] at the bus stop.

grammar.note: Sonst noch etwas? = Anything else?

example_target: Beeil dich, [[sonst]] kommen wir zu spät.

grammar.note: No plural in everyday use.
The person asked is accusative: Ich frage dich. fragen nach = to ask about.
Weak noun: den/dem/des Herrn. Meine Damen und Herren = ladies and gentlemen.
Ich bin dabei! = Count me in!

example_source: Do you have your ID [[with you]]?

grammar.note: das heißt (d. h.) = that is (i.e.).
Accusative niemand(en), dative niemand(em). Opposite: jemand.
Subordinating: the verb goes to the end. Before a noun use the preposition vor.

example_target: Wasch dir die Hände, [[bevor]] du isst.

grammar.note: Colloquially mal: Komm mal her! noch einmal = once more.
Only for questions (direct or indirect); other "when" clauses use wenn or als.
mit etwas fertig sein = to be finished with something; colloquially also "exhausted".

example_source: The food will be [[ready]] in a moment.

grammar.note: Spoken modal particle, like eben. Halt! = Stop!
Not declined. Colloquially also alleine.
Declined like an adjective after an article: die beiden Kinder = the two children.
Plural Sachen also means belongings or clothes.
Hilfe! = Help! The plural is rare.
Declined like der: jeder, jede, jedes; accusative masculine jeden. Alone: jeder = everyone.
Verb + gern = to like doing something. Also gerne.
Replaces über + a thing: über das Problem sprechen → darüber sprechen.
Irregular: du hältst, er hält. halten von = to think of: Was hältst du davon?

example_target: Der Bus [[hält]] direkt vor der Schule.
example_source: The bus [[stops]] right outside the school.

grammar.note: nicht wahr? at the end of a sentence = isn’t it? / right?
Replaces zu + a thing: Ich habe keine Lust dazu = I don’t feel like it.

example_source: Would you like a salad [[with it]]?

grammar.note: Replaces an + a thing: denken an → daran denken. Colloquially dran.
No plural. Vielen Dank! = Thank you very much! Gott sei Dank = thank God.
auf jeden Fall = definitely; für den Fall, dass = in case. Also the grammatical case.
Not declined. Egal! = Whatever! / Never mind!
kennen = to know people, places, things; wissen = to know facts.

example_source: I’ve [[known]] him for a long time.

grammar.note: Irregular: du/er vergisst. Participle without ge-: vergessen.
eine Frage stellen = to ask a question.
Colloquially "really": echt gut = really good. Echt? = Really?

example_source: What do you [[actually]] do for a living?

grammar.note: Irregular: den/dem Namen, but genitive des Namens.
False friend: bekommen = to get, not "to become" (werden). Participle without ge-.
Comparative of spät.
No plural. Glück haben = to be lucky; zum Glück = luckily.
Always declined: der letzte Bus, letzten Sommer.
Replaces auf + a thing: warten auf → darauf warten. Colloquially drauf.
Ende Mai = at the end of May; zu Ende = over, finished.

example_target: Am [[Ende]] der Straße ist ein Café.
example_source: At the [[end]] of the street there’s a café.

grammar.note: Colloquial plural also die Dinger.
Also "to think": Ich meine, du hast recht. Not the possessive mein.
Used when counting; before a noun it is ein/eine: ein Apfel. Es ist eins = It’s one o’clock.

example_target: Der Bus Nummer [[eins]] fährt zum Bahnhof.
example_source: Bus number [[one]] goes to the station.

grammar.note: bereit sein, etwas zu tun = to be willing to do something.
weiter also means "further, on": Mach weiter! = Carry on!

example_target: Ist es noch [[weit]] bis zum Bahnhof?
example_source: Is it still [[far]] to the station?

grammar.note: Keine Ahnung! = No idea!
Usually ein bisschen; not declined.
Possessive for ihr. Drops the e before an ending: eure Kinder, euren Hund.
unter vier Augen = in private.
No plural in everyday use. Singular verb in German: Die Polizei ist da = The police are here.
Irregular: du stirbst, er stirbt. Perfekt with sein. sterben an + dative = to die of.
For location; for direction use nach draußen.
False friend: fast means "almost", not "fast" (schnell).
Colloquial short form of herunter/hinunter.
vorbeikommen = to drop by; an etwas vorbei = past something.
Irregular: du triffst, er trifft. sich treffen = to meet up.
verrückt nach = crazy about.
Dative for position (wo?), accusative for movement (wohin?).
sich Sorgen machen = to worry.
Usually declined: das einzige Problem = the only problem.
Also replaces um + a thing: Es geht darum, ... = It’s about ...
Replaces in + a thing (location). Colloquially drin.

example_target: Hier ist die Dose, die Kekse sind [[darin]].
example_source: Here’s the tin; the biscuits are [[in it]].

grammar.note: As a particle: Komm ruhig rein! = Feel free to come in!
Wie spät ist es? = What time is it?
Also "briefly": Warte kurz! = Wait a moment!
Colloquial. Informal plural also die Kerls.
Position (wo?); the action of putting is legen. In southern Germany and Austria: ist gelegen.

example_source: The book [[is lying]] on the table.

grammar.note: Direct object, no preposition: Ich suche einen Job. suchen nach = to search for.
je ... desto = the ... the: Je früher, desto besser. je nach = depending on.
After a time span: zwei Jahre lang = for two years. The adverb lange = for a long time.
überhaupt nicht = not at all; überhaupt kein = no ... at all.
In exclamations: Was zum Teufel ...? = What the hell ...?

example_source: The fairy tale is about a [[devil]].

grammar.note: Participle without ge-: verloren.
Also "tall" for people: Er ist sehr groß.
aus diesem Grund = for this reason; im Grunde = basically.
Informal; the neutral word is Mutter.
No plural. Lass mich in Ruhe! = Leave me alone!

example_source: I need a bit of [[peace and quiet]].

grammar.note: The plural is rare.
Also a school lesson. For clock times use Uhr: Es ist drei Uhr.
hoffen auf + accusative = to hope for.
For location; for direction use nach oben.
gestern Abend = last night.
With zu + infinitive. Participle without ge-: versucht.
Also "manner": auf diese Art = in this way.

example_source: What [[kind]] of music do you like?

grammar.note: Very common as a term of endearment.
Not the same as etwas. In questions it shows surprise: Bist du etwa krank?
Participle without ge-: erzählt. von etwas erzählen = to tell about something.
Irregular: du läufst, er läuft. Perfekt with sein. Wie läuft es? = How is it going?

example_source: I [[run]] in the park every morning.

grammar.note: Not declined; before a noun use ander-: ein anderes Buch.
The plural is rare; die Wässer = kinds of (mineral) water.
Ordinal of eins; declined like an adjective: der erste Mai, am ersten Tag.
Also "history" (the subject).
ein wenig = a little; wenige (plural) = few.
abholen = to pick someone up.
For words and signs; for what a person means use meinen.
The verb comes right after it: deshalb bleibe ich.

example_target: Es regnet, [[deshalb]] bleiben wir zu Hause.
example_source: It’s raining, [[so]] we’re staying at home.

grammar.note: Declined like der: welcher, welche, welches; accusative masculine welchen.

example_source: [[Which]] film do you want to see?

grammar.note: As an adjective: ein bestimmtes Buch = a particular book.
Drops the c before an ending: ein hoher Berg.
The plural is rare. Not to be confused with der Alte = the old man.

example_target: In deinem [[Alter]] hatte ich kein Handy.
example_source: At your [[age]] I didn’t have a mobile.

grammar.note: Especially common in southern Germany and Austria. Schau mal! = Look!
auf dem Land = in the countryside. Also a German federal state.
Also a train carriage. Southern German plural also die Wägen.

example_target: Er parkt seinen [[Wagen]] vor dem Haus.
example_source: He parks his [[car]] in front of the house.

grammar.note: The thing liked is the subject, the person is dative: Das gefällt mir = I like that.
